text:
mike: Heads up — we just got a support report where a streaming reconnect that crossed regions produced a tiny duplicate charge (few tokens).
elaine: oh no, can you paste the request logs? :eyes:
mike: sure, here's the reconnect window (sanitized):
```
REQUEST id=abc123 session=ses-42 route=eu-1 -> route=us-west-2 reconnect=true prefix_len=120
RESPONSE tokens_charged=15 provisional=true
...client reconnects...
REQUEST id=abc123 session=ses-42 route=us-west-2 reconnect_resume=true prefix_len=120
RESPONSE tokens_charged=5 provisional=false
```
anya: so we're seeing the same prefix counted twice because the route change caused a provisional charge to be re-evaluated?
tim: sounds like a race: eu instance charged provisional on stream termination, then us-west confirmed the tail and also charged confirmed tokens.
elaine: do we currently persist any route ownership on provisional ledger entries?
mike: provisional rows have session_id + short ttl, but route tag isn't strict — they can be re-associated on resume.
anya: hmm. UX question: how should the Console present this? user sees two lines for one request and panics :grimacing:
elaine: propose: Console shows a single logical request row with a "pending reconciliation" badge and a tooltip that explains cross-region reconfirmation. Yellow highlight while provisional. :thinking:
tim: telemetry ask: add a metric for "provisional_flip_rate_by_route_change" so we can measure how often provisional -> confirmed flips across regions. Also histogram of delta tokens.
mike: agree. For short-term mitigation, can we make the router sticky for session->route for N seconds after disconnect? That would avoid cross-route confirmation races.
anya: caveat: stickiness will hurt availability during region failover. We should gate it behind a rollout flag.
elaine: internal API debate: do we change attribution semantics to always attribute to the original route (originating ledger row), or to the final confirmation route? Both have pros/cons for accounting and ops.
tim: my vote: keep confirmer as source-of-truth (final route) but annotate original route on provisional row for easier ops. That way billing aligns with where CPU happened but we can trace origin.
mike: implementation sketch: add `origin_route` to provisional ledger rows, don't change billing math. Also add `route_affinity` header on stream start: `X-Route-Affinity: eu-1;ttl=30s`.
anya: +1 for header. Also add API change: when client resumes, router includes `resume_session_id` and `origin_route` so confirmers can dedupe if session ids match.
elaine: console change: show collapsed row that expands into both provisional and confirmed lines with a reconcile status. Add filter `show_pending=true` for ops.
tim: can we emit an event `billing.reconcile.requested` whenever a provisional is still open > TTL and then closed by a different route? Good for alerting.
mike: I'm going to prototype: router stickiness flag + origin_route annotation + telemetry counters for flips. Will open a PR and a small canary rollout to internal tenants.
anya: thanks — please ping @elaine and @tim on PR. I'll help wire the Console toggle. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: NOTE: customers may see split lines during the roll; docs update recommended (Billing FAQ).
elaine: can we update Billing FAQ to say: "temporary duplicate-looking lines may appear during cross-region reconcilation; final invoice will reflect confirmed tokens" — simple wording.
mike: created draft PR #2345 and added tests for dedupe on session_id + origin_route. Will add telemetry after initial review.
tim: if the prototype looks stable, let's canary 5% of traffic and watch `provisional_flip_rate_by_route_change` for regressions.
anya: sounds good. follow-ups: - PR link, - console mockups, - billing FAQ text. I'll collect and drive the rollout schedule.
elaine: thanks all. I'll schedule a 15m sync if needed. :calendar:
